classification.difficultyReason: Find points from prescribed tangent gradients, then connect tangent–normal geometry with the diagonals of a square.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Find the $x$-coordinates of the points $P$ and $Q$ on $y=(x-7)^2+3$ such that the tangents at $P$ and $Q$ have gradients $1$ and $-1$.

children.label: b
children.prompt: The tangents and normals at $P$ and $Q$ form a square. Show that it has area $0.5$ square units.

spec.description: Editable equation-driven parabola with its two tangents and two normals, unnumbered arrowed axes and labelled points P and Q. Four line colours distinguish the four sides; source mint green is represented by house purple to retain that distinction.
spec.mathematics: Curve y=(x-7)^2+3; P=(15/2,13/4), Q=(13/2,13/4). Tangents y=x-17/4 and y=-x+39/4; normals y=-x+43/4 and y=x-13/4. Their intersections form a square with P and Q as opposite vertices.
spec.answerVisibility: The supplied curve, four lines and point labels remain visible. Numerical coordinates, equations and area are not printed on the question diagram.

answer.short: $PQ=1$ is a diagonal of the square, so $A=\frac12(1)(1)=\frac12=0.5$ square units.
answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}y_P&=\left(\frac{15}{2}-7\right)^2+3\\y_P&=\frac{13}{4}\\y_Q&=\left(\frac{13}{2}-7\right)^2+3\\y_Q&=\frac{13}{4}\end{align*}$$
Thus $P\left(\frac{15}{2},\frac{13}{4}\right)$ and $Q\left(\frac{13}{2},\frac{13}{4}\right)$. The tangent and normal gradients are $1$ and $-1$, giving perpendicular adjacent sides and parallel opposite sides. The opposite vertices $P$ and $Q$ define a diagonal of the square; its other diagonal has the same length.

Since $PQ$ is horizontal:
$$\begin{align*}PQ&=\frac{15}{2}-\frac{13}{2}\\PQ&=1\\A&=\frac12\times1\times1\\A&=\frac12\text{ square units}\\A&=0.5\text{ square units}\end{align*}$$
Alternatively, find the equations of the tangents and normals, their intersection points and the side length of the square, then square the side length. This method takes more working.
